title: Cross-Model KV Cache Transfer in LLM Families: A Closed-Form Linear Mapping for Prefill Reuse
event_hint: Within-family cross-model KV-cache transfer using a closed-form per-head ridge mapper
problem: Model switching for cost-quality cascading, routing, or mid-conversation handoff forces the receiver to re-prefill accumulated context. The paper studies whether a source model's KV cache can be transformed into the target model's format so decoding can skip re-prefill.
mechanism: For matched-KV model pairs, the method fits independent per-target-layer/head ridge regressions from top-k predictive source layers. It strips source RoPE before mapping and re-applies target RoPE, using 500 FineWeb-Edu sequences of 1,024 tokens for calibration; the resulting closed-form mapper is gradient-free and position-independent across supported context lengths.

evidence.claim: On Qwen3 14B→32B, one source layer explains 56% of target-key variance and 32% of value variance; multiple source layers raise these to 79% and 65%.
evidence.source_locator: PDF p.1 abstract; p.2 linear-structure paragraph

evidence.claim: Across six matched-KV pairs in three model families, the linear mapper retains 73–98% of standalone accuracy on the four highest-retention pairs, while two Ministral pairs fall to 42–44% average retention.
evidence.value: 73–98% for four pairs; 42–44% for two pairs
evidence.condition: five accuracy benchmarks; selected k; within-family dense full-attention models

evidence.claim: The mapper runs 4–25x faster small-to-large and 3–7x faster large-to-small than receiver re-prefill across sequence lengths from 64 to 32,768 tokens.
Replacing ridge with an MLP recovers 24.3–36.8 percentage points of HellaSwag retention on the two failure pairs.
The study evaluates only matched-KV, within-family transfer; mismatched-KV pairs and cross-family transfer remain untested.
evidence.condition: six evaluated pairs across Qwen3, Llama 3.1, and Ministral 3

evaluation_context: Experiments cover Qwen3, Llama 3.1, and Ministral 3 dense full-attention families with matched KV-head count and per-head dimension. Accuracy uses ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, MMLU, and GSM8K; multi-turn handoff uses CoQA. Latency appendix measurements use one 8×H100 NVLink node, bf16, 50 warmups and 30 timed trials per cell.
limitations: The method is evaluated only on six matched-KV within-family pairs and does not test mismatched KV dimensions or cross-family transfer. Calibration uses FineWeb-Edu; domain shifts (especially CodeAlpaca) can reduce accuracy. k selection overlaps with some reported benchmarks, and latency measurements use synthetic inputs without measuring end-to-end shipping of the mapped cache to the target process.
project_relevance: This provides a concrete path to avoid repeated prefill when an Agent or serving router switches among same-family models, but requires directional mapper storage and a transferability screen. The sharp Ministral failures and matched-KV restriction make per-pair validation essential before cross-domain deployment.
